messages:
Nadia: Heads up 1: we had a mini-incident where control-plane split + tenant infra churn caused duplicated endpoint manifests and a fail-forward that flipped private endpoints -> public for a subset of requests. Need a design to avoid dual-write races and noisy reconciles.
Tom: Oof. Was that the cross-region controlplane handoff we rolled out last month?
Nadia: Yes, specifically when the regional controlplane accepted a takeover and the global controlplane retried the same change. Both reconciled and triggered route flips.
Ravi: Two immediate ideas: 1) introduce per-tenant operation lease (owner token) so only the lease-holder can apply endpoint changes; 2) have a stable arbitration key derived from controlplane-id + change-id so duplicates are idempotent.
Kara: Owner token makes sense but we also need a fast failover for real outages. Lease TTLs should be short and support manual override for SRE.
Miguel: Agree. Also add a small-state machine for endpoint state: desired -> pending-apply -> verified. Only when verified do we announce route. That reduces visible flapping.
SRE-oncall: From ops standpoint: want a way to mark a tenant into "pause reconciliation" for short windows when customers run infra migrations. Currently we rely on ticketing + manual operator throttles, which scales poorly.
Tom: We can reuse an annotation: `redwood.io/reconcile-mode: auto|paused|manual-queue` and expose an API for infra tools to set/clear.
Nadia: Pseudocode for arbitration (sketch):
```
if lease.holder == this.instance and not lease.expired:
  apply_change()
else if compute_hash(change) == last_applied_hash:
  noop  # idempotent duplicate
else:
  try_acquire_lease()
```
Miguel: We should also consider cross-controlplane event ordering. Add a monotonic change counter stored in tenant metadata (persisted in DB) so any controlplane that loses preemption knows it lost.
Ravi: Operational heuristics: when we detect >K route updates in R seconds for a tenant, flip them into verification-only mode and alert. That prevents chasing a noisy tenant.
Kara: For dedicated customers with SLAs we should offer a "stable-mode" where operator never auto-fails over to public endpoints; instead, issue stuck alerts and page. Default customers get auto-failover with hysteresis.
SRE-oncall: Make sure metrics exist: duplicate_apply_count, lease_acquire_failures, tenant_verification_time. Dashboards and an SLO for verification latency (e.g., 99% < 30s).
Tom: We also need runbook steps for lease contention: commands to force-release lease, to promote follower -> leader, and to reconcile orphaned state.
Nadia: Rollout plan: implement arbitration+lease in operator v3.0 behind feature flag; enable feature flag for non-dedicated tenants in staging; run for 72h; enable for 25% prod tenants; monitor duplicate_apply_count and route-flap metric before wider rollout.
Ravi: Add a migration path for persisted change counter: backfill current sequence numbers with a simple scan job. Job should be idempotent and rate-limited.
Miguel: One more safety net: when we apply a route change, annotate the route with `applied-by` and `applied-at`. If we see conflicting applied-by values in short window, block and escalate.
Kara: Thinking about API ergonomics: expose a "reconcile-suppress-until" TTL on the tenant resource with max 24h and require an operator override for longer. UI should surface who created the suppress.
Tom: For multi-instance operators: leader-election via tenant shards + region affinity reduces cross-instance storms. Combine with token-bucket for apply-rate per region.
deploy-bot: rollout request: private-endpoint-operator v3.0-alpha -> canary :rocket:
SRE-oncall: If we flip to verification-only for a customer, alert routing: dedicated -> pager, non-dedicated -> slack+email. Also include a runbook link in alert.
Nadia: I'll open a design PR with sketches for lease acquisition, idempotency hash, verification states, and the rollout gates. Tagging @Kara @Ravi for review.
Miguel: I'll stub the instrumentation hooks in metrics repo so dashboards are ready when operator ships.
Kara: I'll write the pause/reconcile UI spec and the override flow for SRE.
Nadia: Thanks team. We'll revisit in the architecture sync in 48h with PR link and preliminary canary metrics.
